Room details from the Ricks College Campus Building Histories (Romney 1987 addition housed Math & Computer Science; the Smith Building housed English with carpeted classrooms; the original Spori housed the Art Department until 2000; the Austin Building had electronics labs).

math.place: Romney Building · 3rd floor · Math & Computer Science

followUp.q: In binary, what number does 100 stand for? (shum · seon · senine)

intro.title: Binary, the Nephite way
intro.whisper: Is that the new math teacher?
intro.chair: Class, this is our math candidate. Our computer science students keep tripping on binary. {name}, could you explain it so it finally sticks?
intro.verdict: That's the clearest binary lesson I've seen. I'll recommend you to President Bednar.
intro.thanks: Thank you! I think it finally clicked for them.
intro.frame: Of course. Binary is easier than it looks. Let's look at it through Nephite currency, in Alma 11.

brief.teach: binary, explained with the gold coins of Alma 11. Each coin is one binary digit: holding it is a 1, leaving it out is a 0.
brief.how: each student asks a question about paying with the coins. Answer it, and the chalkboard writes your coins as binary digits (✔ = 1). Answer all the questions to finish the lesson.

followUp.q: Before you correct a fact in someone's writing, what should you do first?
options: Check it against a reliable source
followUp.correct: Check it against a reliable source

intro.title: Editing for accuracy
intro.whisper: Is that the new English teacher?
intro.chair: Class, this is our English candidate. Brother Price has volunteered his write-up of the Kimball Building dedication. {name}, would you show the class how to proofread a paper like this and get it ready to hand in?
intro.verdict: Careful, kind and accurate. I'll recommend you to President Bednar.
intro.thanks: Thank you — and thanks, Brother Price, for being a good sport.
intro.frame: Happy to. Good editing starts with the facts. Let's put Brother Price's page up and check it line by line against the Church News.

brief.teach: how to proofread a paper and get it ready to hand in, using Brother Price's write-up of the Kimball Building dedication.
brief.how: his page is projected on the screen with a few mistakes in it. Move through it word by word, mark each wrong word and choose the correction. Fix every mistake to finish proofreading.

art.place: Original Spori Building · 3rd floor · Art studio

followUp.q: Why does the grid method help you copy a picture?
options: You copy one small square at a time
You never have to look at the picture
followUp.correct: You copy one small square at a time

intro.title: Drawing what you see
intro.chair: Class, meet our art candidate. Our students hold a pencil out at arm's length to measure proportions, and their drawings still come out lopsided. {name}, can you show them a better way? If that old projector cooperates.
intro.verdict: Even with the projector dying, you kept the class drawing. I'll recommend you to President Bednar.
intro.thanks: Thank you! I'm sorry about your projector.
intro.frame: Let's try the grid method. It's like measuring with your pencil, one square at a time. I'll project a picture and we'll copy it square by square. Here's one to try: imagine Rexburg with a temple on the hill someday.

after.text: Well, that projector is finished. Brother Lee, would you carry it over to the electronics lab in the Austin Building? Maybe they can save it.
I hope they can. It's a good old machine.

brief.teach: the grid method, a reliable way to get proportions right: copy a picture one square at a time.
brief.how: the projector shows the picture on the side wall. Paint it onto the drawing board square by square while the class guesses what it is. Get close enough to the picture to pass.

followUp.q: Why do two bulbs in parallel stay bright?
options: Each bulb gets its own path to the battery
followUp.correct: Each bulb gets its own path to the battery

intro.title: Projector repair
intro.whisper: Is that the new engineering teacher?
intro.chair: Class, this is our engineering candidate. Change of plans: a student just carried in the art studio's overhead projector. It shorted out in the middle of their demo this morning. {name}, instead of the lesson you planned, would you fix it in front of the class and explain what went wrong?
intro.verdict: Fixed it live, and they understood why. I'll recommend you to President Bednar.
intro.thanks: Thank you! Let's get this projector back to the art studio.
intro.frame: Happy to. A projector is just a few circuits. I'll open it up on the bench, and we'll follow the path the power takes.

brief.teach: how a short circuit happens and how to fix one, by repairing the art studio's projector live.
brief.how: the projector's wiring is opened up on the bench. Turn the wire tiles so power flows from + through the lamp (and fan) and back to −. Each circuit you fix is one step of the lesson.
